content.text: So we can do the indexing like [z0, z1, z2, time, component, file]

Yes—as a NumPy array, you can arrange it as:

```python
# Each frame: [z0, z1, z2, component]
time_series = np.stack(frames, axis=-2)
# [z0, z1, z2, time, component]

values = np.stack(file_series, axis=-1)
# [z0, z1, z2, time, component, file]
```

Then index with:

```python
values[z0, z1, z2, time, component, file]
```

This cannot currently be stored as one `GData`, because `GData` requires the component axis to be last. It would need either a new collection container or changes to `GData`’s axis model.

So I'd like indexing to work as I have in the example.py. python example.py

    data[:,2:4] *= 5
    ~~~~^^^^^^^
  File "/home/maxwell-rosen/postgkyl/src/postgkyl/gdatastate/gdatastate.py", line 237, in __getitem__
    return self.get_values()[..., comp]
           ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^
IndexError: only integers, slices (`:`), ellipsis (`...`), numpy.newaxis (`None`) and integer or boolean arrays are valid indices

That traceback confirms the issue: `GData.__getitem__` currently treats everything inside `[]` as a component selector and prepends `...`. I’ll update it to support ordinary NumPy multidimensional indexing and in-place slice assignment for interpolated data, while preserving the existing one-argument component shorthand where possible.

content.text: I’m going to make `GData[...]` follow NumPy’s actual axis order: spatial dimensions first, component last. For your `(800, 4)` example, `data[:, 2:4]` will therefore select components 2–3 across every `z0` point, and augmented assignment will mutate the interpolated NumPy-backed dataset. Native Gkeyll-backed data will remain read-only.
